The Perfectly Proportioned Time Only

The iconic Octo Finissimo is now appealing to an even wider audience. Bvlgari has miniaturized the extraordinary, drawing on its expertise in crafting miniature movements, to adorn every wrist with elegance. It isn't just smaller; it's perfectly proportioned, retaining its signature ultra-thin profile and remaining fiercely iconic.

The Octo Finissimo 37 remains true to its heritage with a Grade 5 titanium build, now introduced for the first time in a satin-polished finish. It preserves the soul of the iconic 40 mm model while forging its own path as a more versatile expression, thanks to its reduced size.

The meticulously crafted BVF 100 caliber, born from 3 years of development in Bvlgari's Le Sentier Manufacture, exemplifies the Maison’s art of miniaturization. This new movement is designed to fit perfectly into the sleek dimensions of the watch. It features a 20% reduction in size and a 20% increase in power reserve, bringing it to 72 hours. It has been decorated by hand with radiating Côtes de Genève and Perlage by our watchmakers.

watches.desc:
The new L.U.C 1860 Chronometer : An important tribute to 30 years of “Chopard Manufacture” Fleurier

Chopard introduces a continuation model of the original, iconic L.U.C 1860 to honour the 30th anniversary of Chopard Manufacture in Fleurier. This new edition preserves the spirit of the original model while integrating the technical progress achieved over the past three decades.

Like its predecessor, this new timepiece features a 36.5 mm case, ideal proportions that will delight fine watch collectors. It is crafted in Lucent Steel™ and stands out with its “Areuse Blue” dial – a colour inspired by the Areuse River that flows near the Manufacture in the Val-de-Travers region. This river, known for its dramatic gorges and ever‑changing shades of deep blue, symbolises continuity and connection to nature. Its vivid colours, shaped by light, stone and movement, recall the cool, bright tone used on the dial.

The 18-carat white gold dial is hand‑guilloché with a sunburst pattern, using a vintage guilloché lathe operated by in-house artisans. Additional guilloché rings structure the dial, catching the light and adding depth. A satin‑brushed chapter ring, polished white gold chevron‑shaped hour markers, and Dauphine hands contribute to its overall clarity and harmony. The small seconds subdial at 6 o’clock completes the symmetrical design, which intentionally avoids a date display to preserve purity. The watch is paired with a grey grained calfskin strap.

This timepiece houses the L.U.C Calibre 96.40-L, a direct evolution of the first movement conceived and produced by Chopard Manufacture in Fleurier in 1996. At just 3.30 mm thin, this self‑winding movement incorporates a 22‑carat gold micro‑rotor that efficiently winds two stacked barrels, thanks to Chopard Twin technology, providing a 65-hour power reserve.

The calibre is Poinçon de Genève-certified and Chronometer‑certified (COSC).

specs:

watches.desc:
I began my watchmaking project in 2012. At that time, a vivid memory resurfaced—an antique pocket watch I had once seen, its dial adorned with numerals hand‑engraved by a master craftsman. I wondered whether, by combining modern technology with traditional artisanal skill, it might be possible to create numerals that were even more sculptural and beautiful. That idea ignited something within me. A precisely finished dial, crafted with the latest machining technology, becomes a canvas onto which an engraver carves deeply by hand. Through this fusion, I was able to bring my long‑held vision to life.

In 2018, I founded the company, and in 2019 we began manufacturing and selling our watches. Since then, we have continued to accumulate experience in both production and sales. And gradually, a desire I had kept quietly within me began to burn again.

When I first entered the watch industry in 1990, I was deeply drawn to smaller‑sized watches. I remember clearly how captivated I was by the Patek Philippe Ref.96 and the Breguet Ref.3210—both compact, elegant masterpieces. Although the industry later shifted toward large and thick cases, my dream of creating a watch with a modestly sized case never left me.

The development of our Cal.2524SS movement, introduced in the NH TYPE5 series in 2024, gave me confidence that we could design a small movement capable of placing the small seconds far enough from the center of the dial. With that conviction, I resolved to create a dress watch with a 31 mm screw‑down case.

And now, at last, we have completed the NH TYPE8A. It features our newly developed round hand‑wound movement, Cal.2326SS, housed within a complex three‑piece case equipped with a sapphire exhibition back and a domed sapphire crystal. Naturally, the numerals on the dial—one of the defining characteristics of our watches—are all hand‑engraved by a master engraver.

The TORIC Petite Seconde represents the most essential interpretation of Parmigiani Fleurier’s philosophy. The dial reveals the quiet vibrancy of the hammered surface in Morning Blue, crafted from 18-carat white gold.

The watch is housed in a platinum case with a finely knurled bezel, now echoed by a similarly knurled case back — one of the most distinctive architectural signatures of the TORIC collection.

The movement is structured by two large bridges in solid 18-carat rose gold, decorated with the double hand-guilloché motif. Manually wound, it preserves the tactile ritual that connects the wearer directly to time. The piece is limited to 30 units, individually numbered from 1 to 30.

Previously, the model showcased onyx and lapis lazuli; today, for the very first time, ornamental stone features in the contemporary range on a precious sodalite version. Audemars Piguet is pleased to unveil its new Neo Frame Jumping Hour watch. Inspired by the Streamline design movement, this rectangular timepiece with vertical gadroons debuts the Manufacture’s first selfwinding jumping hour movement, Calibre 7122. Blending horological mastery with vintage aesthetics, this reference presents an entirely novel construction, distinguishable by its pink gold and sapphire case and a strap adorned with a newly developed motif, embodying the spirit of innovation and creativity that has defined Audemars Piguet since its founding.

Blending modern craftsmanship with vintage aesthetics, the model is inspired by a 1929 timepiece (pre-model 1271). At the crossroads of architecture, watchmaking and the reinterpretation of an iconic artistic movement, this new line revives the design codes of the 1930s while harnessing the most advanced technologies in the creation of both case components and movement. Hand-finished in accordance with ancestral savoir-faire, this timepiece embodies the alliance of tradition, audacity and innovation that has been at the heart of the brand for over 150 years.

specs:
Manual-winding mechanical 
Power reserve: 65 h, 28800 vph 
Skeleton movement
watches.desc:
Conceived in the spirit of La Montre Objet d’Art, the DANIEL ROTH Extra Plat Rose Gold Skeleton reinterprets Extra Plat through the art of skeletonisation. While preserving the refined proportions and architectural purity of the iconic double-ellipse case, the watch fully reveals the new calibre DR002SR.

Both the thin 6.9mm case and the movement are crafted in solid 5N rose gold, forming a luminous composition of warm metallic tones, suspended negative space, and hand-finished surfaces in perfect architectural harmony. The decision to craft the components and case in gold was driven by both technical and aesthetic considerations, providing clarity to the handcrafted work and paying homage to traditional finishing.

The manually wound DR002SR is entirely manufactured in-house at La Fabrique du Temps Louis Vuitton. Its bridges and mainplates are completely redesigned for skeletonisation, creating a movement architecture defined by lightness and transparency, without compromising rigidity or chronometric performance.

Each bridge is meticulously bevelled by hand, revealing polished angles that capture light from every angle. The DR002SR is further distinguished by numerous sharp internal angles - among the most demanding expressions of traditional haute horlogerie finishing – that are impossible to execute by machine.

Traditional watchmaking techniques and legibility remained central to the construction of the Extra Plat Rose Gold Skeleton, where a philosophy of “less is more” allows the tone-on-tone finishing and the movement's depth to emerge with proportional clarity and elegance.

watches.name: Hand-engraved Manual-winding Spring Drive
watches.functions: Hours, Minutes, Seconds, Power reserve indicator
specs: Hours, Minutes, Seconds, Power reserve indicator
watches.desc:
In the heart of the Shinshu region of central Japan, the majestic Tateshina Waterfall flows in a primeval forest, its presence embodying the eternal rhythm of nature. Inspired by this sylvan scene, the latest Spring Drive creation from Grand Seiko’s Masterpiece Collection expresses time not as an abstraction, but as a natural, continuous flow.

Brought to life through exquisite hand engraving

A limited edition of 50, each example features a dial that is individually hand-engraved, bringing each surface to life through exceptional craftsmanship. Lines radiate and intersect in multiple directions to evoke the dynamic movement of water as it springs from the earth and cascades over rocks. Translating this flowing expression – from its emergence to its descent - from dial to case required a careful reconciliation between the designer’s vision and the engraver’s hand, ensuring that the motif retained both continuity and vitality without becoming repetitive.

Beautifully finished and expertly engineered

At the heart of this watch lies the manual-winding Spring Drive Caliber 9R02, designed, finished, and assembled by the elite craftsmen and women of the Micro Artist Studio, located in Seiko Epson’s facility in Shiojiri, Nagano Prefecture. Measuring just 4.0mm thick – the thinnest of any Spring Drive movement – Caliber 9R02 achieves its remarkably slim profile while providing a power reserve of 84 hours. This is achieved through the Dual Spring Barrel and a unique mechanism known as the Torque Return System. The movement’s bridges are hand-finished to an exceptionally high standard, with mirror-polished edges and finely textured surfaces creating a striking contrast. Every detail, visible or not, reflects the same pursuit of precision and beauty that defines the exterior of the watch.

Inspired by an iconic Grand Seiko design

The movement is housed in a Platinum 950 case inspired by the iconic 44GS design. Its slim, 9.6mm profile is brought to life through engraved patterns that interact with Zaratsu-polished planes, revealing an ever-changing interplay of light and shadow. The smooth, silent glide of the Spring Drive seconds hand further mirrors the uninterrupted flow of time in nature.

Every element of this creation reflects the philosophy of the Masterpiece Collection: that true simplicity demands the highest level of mastery. Rather than merely displaying the time, this watch embodies it—through nature, craftsmanship, and the enduring beauty of precision.

watches.name: SP One Platinum
specs:
Manual-winding mechanical 
Power reserve: 72 h, 18000 vph 
Skeleton movement
watches.desc:
What if MB&F created an elegant 38mm watch?

The MB&F SP One, initially dubbed "Three Circles", showcases a trinity of floating elements – the barrel, balance wheel, and dial – defying gravity on your wrist. These components appear to hover mysteriously at the centre of an amphitheatre, all visible through invisible sapphire domes, with the balance wheel performing a mid-air dance and the tilted dial highlighting MB&F’s clever conical gearing.

Encased in a 38mm pebble-like shell, the SP One melds a smooth, tactile feel with a bezel-free design and delicately detached lugs. As MB&F’s slimmest and smallest watch, it nonetheless remains true to the brand’s signature three-dimensional architecture and boundary-pushing spirit. Somewhere between MB&F’s radical Horological Machines and more classic Legacy Machines, the SP One inaugurates a new, undefinable “Special Projects” collection.

The SP One movement is crafted around the three key elements of any mechanical watch: the barrel, the balance wheel, and the dial. Each component isn’t just there for show; they’re meant to feel like they’re floating in mid-air. It’s the thoughtful architecture of the movement that truly enhances this captivating levitation effect: most components are cleverly hidden beneath the three key elements, letting their beauty take centre stage.

Visually, the three elements have identical circumferences, adding complexity to the movement's design. The single-barrel architecture is elegantly suspended, enhancing the levitation effect and presenting a genuine challenge for the movement designers. The balance wheel oscillates at 2 o’clock and captivates the wearer's eyes like a flying saucer. The dial is tilted just right to highlight MB&F's expertise in conical gearing.

Surrounding this movement is the “amphitheatre”: a bevelled flange that spotlights the intricacies of the movement.

Flip the SP One over, and you'll uncover the hand finishing and overall attention to detail typical of MB&F. The wheels are hand-angled, with prominent chatons, and the finish balance is subtle between satin, polished, and micro-blasted surfaces.

In essence, a classical MB&F that has nothing classical about it.

watches.name: Tonda PF Minute Rattrapante Arctic Rose
specs:
Self-winding mechanical 
Power reserve: 48 h, 21600 vph

Hours, Minutes, Retrograde Minutes 
Two superimposed minute hands
watches.desc:
In 2023, Parmigiani Fleurier unveiled the Tonda PF Minute Rattrapante, a world first that immediately captivated connoisseurs. Not a complication created to measure performance, but a timepiece offering a unique kind of experience, the ability to add time on demand. An innovative idea executed with disarming clarity, bringing watchmaking back to its original purpose: to be a lifelong companion.

Its principle, unmatched to this day, is one of remarkable clarity: two superimposed minute hands, invisible to one another until the function is activated. Through this ingenious construction, a highly sophisticated mechanism becomes intuitive, transforming complexity into elegance. Three pushers orchestrate the function: one at 10 o’clock to add a minute, another at 8 o’clock to add five, and the crown to reset. The rhodium-plated hand indicates the real time. The rose gold hand marks the chosen interval. When the two hands meet again, the granted time has elapsed.

watches.name: L'Impétrant
watches.functions: Hours, Minutes, Power reserve indicator, Retrograde Hours, Retrograde Minutes, Jumping hours
specs:
Manual-winding mechanical 
Power reserve: 70 h, 18000 vph 
Skeleton movement
Hours, Minutes, Power reserve indicator, Retrograde Hours, Retrograde Minutes, Jumping hours
watches.desc:
L’Impétrant is a timepiece built around a fundamental idea: making movement visible, because movement is the very expression of life.

This inaugural creation by Stéphane Pierre places dynamism at the heart of its identity. Hours and minutes are displayed by two long retrograde hands sweeping across ceramic dials. After twelve hours of progression, they simultaneously return to their starting point in a motion that is both spectacular and playful, transforming the reading of time into a true mechanical performance.

At the centre of this composition, the balance wheel is displayed dial-side and elevated to emphasise the movement’s depth. As the beating heart of the watch, it visually punctuates the passage of time while reinforcing the sense of life that animates the piece.

L’Impétrant is powered by a hand-wound calibre developed entirely in-house. Its 11.5 mm balance wheel oscillates at 2.5 Hz, favouring the visual expression of its beats. The 70-hour power reserve is indicated by a vertical cone visible on the dial side and complemented by a display on the reverse side of the watch, while a Maltese cross stopwork system helps preserve chronometric stability throughout the useful operating range of the movement.

Housed in a 39 mm Grade 23 titanium case, l’Impétrant Titanium combines lightness, technical sophistication and elegance.

Its name, borrowed from submarine terminology, resonates with its creator’s journey and the spirit of this first independent horological creation.

watches.name: Inspiration One

specs:
Manual-winding mechanical 
Power reserve: 36 h, 18000 vph
Hours, Minutes, Seconds, Power reserve indicator, Special escapement
watches.desc:
The Inspiration One is the timepiece that inaugurates the CLEGUER brand. Its apparent simplicity belies a high degree of technical complexity in the service of chronometry. Created by Mathieu CLEGUER in collaboration with designer Lee Yuen-Rapati.

Housed in a 38.5 mm white gold case, the Inspiration One features a multidimensional dial where the movement itself becomes a visual landscape. Key elements include: a grand feu champlevé enamel dial set off-center at 2 o'clock, a snailed barrel highlighted by a 36-hour power reserve indicator, and an oversized balance wheel measuring 12.9 mm and beating at 18,000 vibrations per hour.

On the reverse side, the gear train and ratchet topped with a Maltese cross stop work are revealed, the latter limits power reserve but ensures consistent chronometric performance from first to last second.

The centerpiece is the Innate escapement, a modern reinterpretation of the natural escapement. After five years of research and development, a solution was found to make this 200-year-old concept self-starting by replacing direct impulse transmission with an indirect, tangential system. Locking and impulse for both wheels are now performed on a central lever, enhancing efficiency and perfecting the experience with the addition of a hacking second.

A modern architecture showcasing an innovative solution while retaining the codes of traditional watchmaking.

watches.name: Time Jumper
specs:
Self-winding mechanical 
Power reserve: 55 h, 28800 vph 
Skeleton movement
watches.desc:
Concept & Creative Context

The Time Jumper marks a decade since the revival of Czapek & Cie, and it celebrates this milestone in the most Czapek way possible: by going against the expected. Rather than unveiling an elaborate grand complication, the Maison chose to reimagine the most fundamental act in watchmaking — the expression of time itself.

The creative impulse draws a direct line between past and future. François Czapek, the great 19th-century Genevan watchmaker, was a master of the pocket watch: the half-hunter case, the round form, the art of guillochage. The Time Jumper reclaims all three, then projects them into a retro-futuristic vision shaped by science fiction, spatial exploration, and Czapek's signature philosophy: head in the sky, feet on the ground.

The result is a 40.5mm "flying saucer" in stainless steel with a white gold guilloché inlay — smooth, aerodynamic, almost without a straight line. Designed by Thomas Funder in close collaboration with the Maison, the case plays on the tension between symmetry and asymmetry, beauty and strangeness that has always defined Czapek's aesthetic. The half-hunter cover is engraved with an entirely new three-dimensional guilloché motif — an exclusive registered pattern created by Czapek's longstanding partner Metalem, evolved from the Singularité guilloché of the Antarctique Tourbillon. It creates a striking optical illusion: curves spiralling into a deep black hole, its event horizon formed by a bubble-shaped loupe positioned directly above the dial crystal. Through this loupe, the hours spring into view. Open the cover, and the entire open-worked movement is revealed beneath a sapphire glass.

Technical Characteristics

At the heart of the Time Jumper beats Calibre 10.01, the first expression of Czapek's new in-house Calibre 10 platform — a self-winding movement designed not as an endpoint but as a foundation for the next decade of complications, each of which will be fully integrated rather than modularly stacked.

The complication is a jumping hour displayed on a 24-hour register across two sapphire discs (one for units, one for tens), accompanied by trailing minutes on a rotating peripheral ring. Displaying 24 hours on two independent discs simultaneously is a première, protected by a patent-pending mechanism. The 24-hour register was chosen deliberately: the flying saucer form evokes an astronaut's instrument, for which a 24-hour display is natural.

The centrally mounted winding rotor in recycled 950 platinum is skeletonised to reveal the architecture beneath. Its arms echo the shape of a geometry compass, attached to the central axis with geometric precision. The five-spoke wheels, diamond-bevelled, are an exclusive Czapek signature. Rhodium-coated bridges contrast with blackened plates to create a play of light evoking the depths of space. Hours are filled with Super-Luminova; the minutes disc is laser-coloured in blue. The movement was designed, conceived and assembled in-house, with 75% of its components machined internally.

The piece is issued as a limited edition of 100 in stainless steel, part of an overall production of 180 Calibre 10.1 movements — a figure chosen to honour the 180th anniversary of the founding of Czapek & Cie in Geneva in 1845.

watches.name: Pulse60 Titanium Black
watches.functions: Hours, Minutes, Seconds, Power reserve indicator
specs:
Manual-winding mechanical 
Power reserve: 96 h, 7200 vph

Hours, Minutes, Seconds, Power reserve indicator 
Natural half dead-beat seconds
watches.desc:
Ultra-amplitude:
pushing mechanical limits

Dominique Renaud has already pushed the boundaries of the regulating organ under extreme conditions, demonstrating his spirit of exploration and invention. His explorations have shown that it is possible to break away from conventional watchmaking standards and rethink the way a balance wheel interacts with its escapement.

The Pulse 60 explores the uncharted territory of low frequencies, featuring the lowest frequency found in contemporary mechanical watchmaking: 1Hz. Its balance wheel oscillates just 60 times per minute – the same frequency as a human heart at rest. This exceptional frequency reduces the number of impulses and shocks to the escapement, thereby limiting the disturbances that disrupt the balance wheel’s movement. The seconds are marked by a single oscillation of the balance wheel, around which the rest of the movement is organised.

A large balance wheel to master the second

In the Pulse 60, the construction of the balance wheel, plate and escape pin assembly has been completely redesigned to allow an amplitude of over 360° without rebattement, something that was impossible in a traditional design.

More than just a feat of geometry, this amplitude has a direct impact on how the balance wheel is regulated, as it remains free for longer and over a greater distance. During this extended period, its movement is governed by its own dynamic laws, rather than by interactions with the escapement, which helps to make the timekeeping more stable and less sensitive to micro-variations.

Consequently, the number of disturbances experienced by the balance wheel is reduced to a minimum. The remarkable stability that results brings the watch’s behaviour closer to that of an ideal oscillator.

watches.name: CIC 39 InVerto Titanium
specs:
Manual-winding mechanical 
Power reserve: 40 h, 21600 vph
watches.desc:
MAKING THE INVISIBLE VISIBLE

For centuries, watchmakers have pursued the same objective: to make the measurement of time ever more consistent. Yet the mechanisms developed in pursuit of this goal generally remain invisible, concealed behind dials and bridges.

With the CIC 39 InVerto Titanium, Bernhard Lederer offers a different perspective. The double remontoir d’égalité becomes the true protagonist of the timepiece. The InVerto does not simply display the time: it reveals the complex mechanics that ensure its regularity.

AN INVERTED ARCHITECTURE DEDICATED TO CHRONOMETRY

The InVerto takes its name from its unique inverted construction. The movement was entirely reimagined to reveal, on the dial side, the components that contribute directly to the stability of the energy supply and the precision of the watch.

This three-dimensional construction makes it possible to visually follow the flow of energy through the movement. The two remontoirs d’égalité now take centre stage, surrounded by the transmission and regulating organs.

Far from being a mere stylistic exercise, this architecture expresses a fundamental conviction: the mechanisms that make chronometry possible deserve to be observed, understood and admired.

THE DOUBLE REMONTOIR: ONE OF HAUTE HORLOGERIE’S RAREST COMPLICATIONS

At the heart of the CIC 39 InVerto Titanium lies Bernhard Lederer’s patented double remontoir d’égalité complication. Among the rarest complications in haute horlogerie, it is also exceptionally complex to design, manufacture and regulate. The system relies on two separate remontoirs operating independently of one another.

First introduced within the Central Impulse Chronometer (CIC), this mechanism enables each remontoir to release every fifteen seconds, delivering remarkably consistent energy to the escapement. Much of its complexity lies in the precise synchronisation of the two mechanisms.

Entirely developed and manufactured at the LEDERER Manufacture in Saint-Blaise, this complication forms one of the foundations of the watch’s chronometric construction. Its perfectly sequenced operation also becomes one of the principal mechanical animations revealed by the InVerto.

To limit the energy required for their release and reduce friction, the remontoirs’ control mechanism has been positioned on the axis of the third wheel. Together, the two remontoirs ensure a constant supply of energy, helping the balance maintain a stable amplitude throughout the entire power reserve.

Far more than a visual demonstration, the double remontoir d’égalité represents one of the most accomplished expressions of Bernhard Lederer’s four decades of research into energy transmission and mechanical precision.

THE LEGACY OF MARINE CHRONOMETERS

The energy delivered by the two remontoirs powers the double-wheel detent escapement developed by Bernhard Lederer, featuring two independent escape wheels.

Historically used in the finest marine chronometers for its exceptional chronometric performance, the detent escapement is renowned for its high efficiency and the minimal disturbance it exerts on the oscillator. Bernhard Lederer reinterpreted this historic principle to meet the demands of a contemporary wristwatch. Combined with the double remontoir system, it forms one of the foundations of the chronometric architecture that defines the CIC 39 InVerto Titanium.

TITANIUM AS A NATURAL EXTENSION OF INNOVATION

Crafted from Grade 5 titanium, the CIC 39 InVerto Titanium combines mechanical innovation with contemporary wearing comfort.

The material’s lightness enhances the experience on the wrist, while its technical character naturally complements the movement’s modern architecture. The contrast between the contemporary case and the entirely hand-executed finishing illustrates the balance between traditional craftsmanship and horological innovation.

A VISION OF INDEPENDENT WATCHMAKING

Entirely developed and manufactured at the LEDERER Manufacture in Saint-Blaise, the CIC 39 InVerto Titanium embodies the vision Bernhard Lederer has pursued for more than forty years: to explore the fundamental principles of watchmaking, challenge established solutions and develop new approaches capable of advancing chronometry while keeping the true art of watchmaking alive.

Every component, every technical solution and every finish contributes to the same ambition: to reveal the principles that allow the measurement of time to remain consistent.

The CIC 39 InVerto Titanium does not merely tell the time.

It reveals chronometry.

watches.desc:
The UR-FREAK is a limited-edition reimagining of Ulysse Nardin’s Freak, considered by many to be one of the most important contemporary contributions to horology. The UR-FREAK was designed in collaboration with the imaginative minds of two pioneering independent Swiss watchmakers. URWERK and Ulysse Nardin who are vanguards in their own respect and worked together for the first time to create the UR-FREAK.

- The first collaboration between URWERK and Ulysse Nardin.

- Mechanics define the design: fusion of the iconic wandering hour satellite of URWERK and the Ulysse Nardin Freak.

- Ulysse Nardin’s Freak rotates the movement to tell the time; URWERK’s hour satellite bends mechanics and reshapes our perception of time itself.

- Two complex mechanisms are fused into a single, fully integrated, in-house caliber.

watches.desc:
BEHRENS x Vianney Halter : Master Collection KWH

Chinese high-end independent watchmaking brand BEHRENS has partnered with master watchmaker Vianney Halter to unveil the latest Master Cellection KWH limited edition.
The inspiration for the Master Collection KWH watch came from a visit to Halter’s workshop. BEHRENS founder Lin Bingqiang noticed an antique electricity meter in Halter’s collection, which echoed a similar industrial artifact he owned. This moment of serendipity sparked the idea of translating the aesthetics of vintage industrial instruments into a modern watch design.
The design draws inspiration from the antique electricity meter, an icon of 20th century industrial civilization. Its square form and mechanical logic are reinterpreted into a compact case, transforming industrial elements into a contemporary horological expression.
Further creative exchanges introduced another layer of inspiration: the classic video games Snake and Tetris.

The watch is powered by the in-house Behrens Caliber BM06 manual-winding movement, co-developed and co-created by BEHRENS and Vianney Halter. Comprising 870 components, it features dual mainspring barrels and delivers approximately 72 hours of power reserve.

The hour display draws inspiration from the classic pixel game Snake, adding a sense of playful nostalgia. This display incorporates BEHRENS’ patented ruby-bearing micro-chain mechanical system, along with a temperature-compensation mechanism to ensure stable performance across varying conditions.
The dial features a circular axle display system. The left axle integrates a power reserve indicator and day-night display, while the right axle indicates minutes. On the caseback, a calendar and moonphase are positioned at 12 o’clock, supported by quick-adjust buttons on the case.

The case is crafted from pioneering materials tantalum alloy and the mechanism is boasted with a deep Lazuline Blue finish. The tantalum alloy offers high hardness, excellent corrosion resistance, and strong mechanical performance. Its naturally dark metallic tone delivers a refined, understated aesthetic. The Lazuline Blue a deep, cool shade that enhances the metal’s natural character, creating a balanced expression of modern sophistication.

Combining industrial design that carries the memory of time with mechanical infrastructure that awakens childhood wonder, they carve out an intimate realm on the wrist.

About Behrens

Founded in 2012 in Shenzhen, China, Behrens is an independent high-end watch brand with full in-house capabilities. Since its inception, the brand has stayed true to its mission of innovating through mechanical art. With a steady stream of creative horological concepts, Behrens has established itself as a modern independent manufacturer with global influence.
Since its founding, BEHRENS has continuously explored the boundaries of watchmaking materials with the spirit of innovation. By expanding beyond conventional applications, the brand brings new depth and diversity to contemporary horology.

About Vianney Halter

Vianney Halter is one of the most celebrated independent watchmakers of his generation. A member of the Académie Horlogère des Créateurs Indépendants (AHCI) since 2000, he was awarded Best Watchmaker at the Grand Prix d’Horlogerie de Genève (GPHG) in 2011. His works are recognised for their revolutionary mechanical structures and futuristic design language, earning him international acclaim.

Halter’s mechanical aesthetics and philosophy align closely with BEHRENS’ vision of blending innovation with the artistry of traditional watchmaking.

watches.desc:
The Grande Double Sonnerie is powered by a fully integrated movement and represents the most ambitious achievement ever undertaken by Blancpain, as well as the most complicated watch in Blancpain’s history. Developed over eight years, it is comprised of 1,053 components within the Calibre 15GSQ (1,116 components in total), the result of more than 1,200 technical drawings and 21 patents developed throughout the project, 13 of which are incorporated into the final movement.

This creation introduces a world first in the field of grande sonnerie wristwatches: the ability to select, at the push of a button, between two distinct melodies performed by a four-note, four-hammer striking mechanism. Alongside the traditional Westminster chime, the watch offers an original composition created exclusively for Blancpain by musician Eric Singer. Unlike conventional grande sonneries, which rely on two tones, the Grande Double Sonnerie employs four perfectly tuned notes (E, G, F and B), opening the door to true melodic expression. Noteworthy as compared with other sonneries, on the hour, it performs all four quarters following the striking of the hours, delivering one of the most elaborate musical sequences ever integrated into a wristwatch.

Acoustic performance was the subject of dedicated development. A patented acoustic membrane integrated into the bezel enhances sound transmission, while a silent magnetic regulator ensures exceptional tempo stability without generating parasitic noise. Far more than a quest for acoustic power, the development of the Grande Double Sonnerie focused on achieving true musicality. For the first time in watchmaking history, the partial frequencies of each note were studied and mastered in order to create a sound signature of exceptional richness and harmony. The result of a close collaboration between the Manufacture’s laboratory and its master watchmakers, each gong is adjusted by hand through successive refinements measured to the micron. Combining scientific analysis with artisanal expertise, this painstaking tuning process continues until every note reaches perfect pitch and blends harmoniously with the whole, transforming the watch into a true mechanical musical instrument.

Beyond the striking functions of grande sonnerie, petite sonnerie, minute repeater without the need for prior arming, the 15GSQ includes a 4 Hz flying tourbillon with a silicon balance spring, a fully integrated retrograde perpetual calendar, and dual power reserve indicators dedicated respectively to the movement and the striking mechanism.

The flying tourbillon, a direct descendant of Blancpain’s 1989 invention - the world’s first flying tourbillon wristwatch - has been updated with a 4 Hz frequency and a silicon balance spring, enhancing chronometric stability, resistance to magnetism, and isochronism.

The retrograde perpetual calendar is an entirely new construction for this caliber. Unlike the modular constructions commonly found in grand complications, it is fully integrated into the movement architecture to preserve the visibility of the striking mechanism and achieve a thin profile. Blancpain’s patented under-lug correctors have also been re-engineered and incorporated directly into the movement, enabling tool-free adjustment while preserving the watch’s acoustic performance.

Five safety mechanisms protect all functions against incorrect handling.

Despite its extreme level of complexity, the watch remains remarkably wearable, measuring 47 mm in diameter and only 14.5 mm in thickness. Like all Blancpain timepieces, it has undergone extensive shock and fatigue testing, underscoring its vocation as a watch intended to be worn every day.

Beyond its technical achievements, the Grande Double Sonnerie is also the result of an extraordinary collective endeavour that mobilised the full breadth of Blancpain’s expertise over a period of eight years. Laboratory engineers, acoustic specialists, movement constructors, technical office teams, prototyping experts, complication watchmakers and the master decorators of La Ferme du Brassus worked together to push the boundaries of traditional striking watchmaking and transform a horological mechanism into a genuine miniature musical instrument. This constant collaboration between scientific innovation, precision engineering and traditional craftsmanship was essential to the creation of a timepiece unlike any other.

Among the many areas of expertise brought together to create the Grande Double Sonnerie, that of master wachmakers Romain and Yoann holds a distinctive place. With more than a decade of experience within the Manufacture and deep expertise in striking watches, they contributed to the development of the assembly methods and specialised tooling required for the project. Each movement requires nearly a full year of work and is assembled, adjusted and completed from A to Z individually by each one of them. Upon completion, each watchmaker signs the movement’s gold plaque, making every timepiece the expression of a level of craftsmanship that is both highly personal and truly exceptional.

The finishing meets the most demanding standards of traditional haute horlogerie. The mainplate and 26 bridges are crafted from 18-carat gold and decorated entirely by hand. The movement features 135 inward angles, whose execution required the expertise of Blancpain’s Métiers d’Art artisans. To achieve this exceptional level of finishing, they employed techniques and tools derived from the art of engraving, including the "burin". The movement is further enhanced by perlage, mirror polishing, hand-beveling, satin finishing and decorative treatments applied to both visible and hidden surfaces, the execution of which required the development and manufacture of more than 200 dedicated tools.

Produced at a rate of only two pieces per year and entirely designed, manufactured, decorated and assembled in-house in the Vallée de Joux, the Grande Double Sonnerie marks a major milestone in the history of striking watches by bringing together, for the first time, acoustic innovation, musicality, grand complication watchmaking and artisanal excellence within a single creation.

L.U.C Grand Strike – The Sound of Eternity

Chopard Manufacture in Fleurier celebrates its 30th anniversary with its most complicated chiming watch to date

From the workshops of Chopard Manufacture comes the new L.U.C Grand Strike, an opus of mechanical mastery developed entirely within the walls of the Swiss watchmaker. This exceptional chiming timepiece, featuring a grande sonnerie, petite sonnerie and minute repeater with proprietary sapphire crystal gongs, represents the culmination of the Maison’s mechanical expertise and a decades-long sonnerie journey initiated by Karl-Friedrich Scheufele, Co-President of Chopard.

The result of over 11,000 hours of focused research and development, the L.U.C Grand Strike draws on ten proprietary technical patents - five of which were newly developed for this timepiece - making it the most complex watch ever created by Chopard Manufacture. Its performance is assured by rigorous in-house tests as well as certifying bodies such as the Poinçon de Genève, and the Contrôle Officiel Suisse des Chronomètres (COSC). With these certifications, the L.U.C Grand Strike is officially the most comprehensively rated grande sonnerie among contemporary high complications.

The design of this timepiece is a blend of traditional forms with modern aesthetics, combining understated curves with a dial-less display that puts the 686-component calibre L.U.C 08.03-L in the spotlight. The lower half of the watch dial is occupied by a 60-second tourbillon, a visual reminder of the COSC-certified performance of the movement. A hallmark of watchmaking excellence and innovation at Chopard, the patented sapphire crystal gongs are machined in one single unit with the dial. This unique gong construction, using the horologically unprecedented material of sapphire crystal, is what gives the L.U.C Grand Strike its matchless acoustic character.

“It has always been our intention to conceive a grande sonnerie at Chopard. If you look at the L.U.C Grand Strike, what you see is the cumulative impact of 30 years spent creating and innovating in the domain of fine watchmaking. When you listen to its chime, you are hearing the rhythm of Haute Horlogerie at Chopard Manufacture. If the chime moves you, it’s because you resonate with our way of making watches” explains Karl-Friedrich Scheufele.

The Grand Planetarium Eccentric is the first and only mechanical wristwatch capable of displaying the real-time orbits of all eight planets in our Solar System, from Mercury all the way out to Neptune.

The case is machined from 316L stainless steel and then subjected to low-temperature carbon diffusion, a process that raises surface hardness to roughly 1,200 Vickers — about six times that of untreated steel. The case is finished with bead-blasting, giving it a matte, gray-toned surface that diffuses light, which makes what little wear that does occur far less conspicuous. It measures 44mm wide and 14.3mm high

The dial is composed of nine pieces of oxidized silicon, producing shifting blue-violet interference colours that evoke the depths of space.

Across its surface, hand-painted Super-LumiNova planets trace their real orbital periods — from Mercury’s 87.97 days to Neptune’s 164.80 years — forming a miniature mechanical model of the Solar System.

Naissance d’une Montre 3 is a horological heritage project with an important human dimension representing the culmination of six years’ work. The result is a timekeeper conceived for the wrist, officially chronometer-certified by the COSC and handcrafted using traditional tools, without digital assistance.

Constant force via a fusee-and-chain transmission system, bimetallic balance, central seconds hand, open structure: its technical and aesthetic characteristics are deeply rooted in the heritage of the Master Watchmaker, Ferdinand Berthoud.

As expected, the 11 “Naissance d'une Montre 3” chronometers meet the same quality and finishing criteria as any other contemporary timepieces from Chronométrie Ferdinand Berthoud. They offer vivid proof that what truly counts is the journey rather than the destination – and that this journey is shaped by the passing of time, the “temps qui instruit” [Dedicated to time, the great teacher] in the words of Louis Berthoud, Ferdinand Berthoud’s nephew.

Coinciding with the tenth anniversary of Chronométrie Ferdinand Berthoud, the presentation of Naissance d'une Montre 3 is the outcome of an ambitious dream nurtured by its founder and President Karl-Friedrich Scheufele. This outstanding cross-disciplinary project drew on the expertise of more than 80 artisans and specialists from Chronométrie Ferdinand Berthoud and Chopard to create a contemporary watch, entirely handcrafted and inspired by Ferdinand Berthoud's Astronomical Pocket Watch No. 3.

The result is a series of 11 contemporary timepieces, powered by a unique combination of a split bimetallic temperature-compensated Guillaume-type balance wheel and a constant-force fusee-and-chain transmission system. Entirely visible from the dial side, this movement is housed a new 44 mm-diameter 18-carat gold case, especially conceived on this occasion.

A great deal of patience and time were devoted to bringing this piece of horological art to life. The creation of a dedicated workshop regrouping vintage machine tools and run by a passionate team of micro-mechanical engineers made it possible to produce the raw components without compromising on precision criteria and quality standards.

In accordance with the regulations governing the Time Æon Foundation, each component of Naissance d'une Montre 3 has been individually crafted without digital assistance, entirely by hand or using traditional tools guided by the human eye, hand and mind.

After 11,000 hours of work and six years of dedication, the first result of this extraordinary project was born. Produced exclusively for Phillips in association with Bacs & Russo in Geneva, this unique piece in stainless steel was sold on November 8, 2025 for an exceptional amount of CHF 1,270,000, thus confirming collectors’ strong interest in this extraordinary project.

The next ten, made of 18-carat ethical gold, will be produced at a rate of two per year starting in 2026 and thus pursuing the intense collaboration between the artisans at Chronométrie Ferdinand Berthoud and Chopard.

watches.desc:
With the Endeavour Minute Repeater Cylindrical Tourbillon Skeleton Cosmic Rain, H. Moser & Cie. reinterprets one of its most complex creations in a limited edition of 20 pieces, where horological excellence meets the artistic crafts. Housed in a 40 mm titanium case, this exceptional timepiece combines a minute repeater displayed on the dial side, a flying tourbillon equipped with a cylindrical hairspring, and a fully skeletonised hand-wound movement. Complementing this technical feat is an artistic dimension embodied by a miniature aventurine dial adorned with delicate mother-of-pearl inlays. Bridging sound, motion and light, this creation explores the many facets of watchmaking artistry and celebrates the meeting of tradition, innovation and artisanal craftsmanship.

In this exceptional timepiece, the minute repeater takes centre stage. The hammers and gongs, traditionally concealed on the reverse side of the movement, are revealed on the dial side. This distinctive construction required a complete rethinking of the calibre’s architecture in order to deliver impeccable acoustic performance while offering an unobstructed view of the mechanism. The beauty of the chime is matched by that of the movement itself, unveiled through meticulous skeletonisation. Openworked bridges, lightened structures and uninterrupted sightlines invite the eye to travel freely through the calibre.

At 2 o’clock, interrupting this transparency, a domed aventurine subdial immediately captures attention with its depth and visual richness. For this creation, fragments of aventurine glass in two different colours are applied by hand onto a domed base to create H. Moser & Cie.’s signature fumé gradient, before undergoing multiple “Grand Feu” firings.

Once this first stage is complete, the dial is subjected to a second, exceptionally delicate artistic process. Fine strips of mother-of-pearl are cut, subtly curved and carefully set into a pre-engraved surface, following the contours of the dial. Their softly iridescent glow appears to drift through the depths of the aventurine like a shower of stars across a night sky. Each individual strip is positioned by hand, transforming this miniature dial into a unique composition where glass, light and matter converge.

This artistic work does not compete with the mechanics; it complements them. While the minute repeater speaks to the ear and the tourbillon expresses the precision of motion, the aventurine and mother-of-pearl captivate the eye. Three distinct languages united within a single creation.

specs: The dial is an integral part of the case

Manual-winding mechanical

watches.desc:
ThinKing Mystery is the culmination of Konstantin Chaykin’s many years of work in one of the most demanding niches of contemporary independent watchmaking. Today, with a case thickness of just 1.65 mm, it remains the thinnest mechanical watch ever produced as an ultra-limited collection. This world record is founded on several patented inventions.

The first is a double balance with toothed coupling. In a traditional balance assembly, components are stacked vertically: the rim, hairspring, impulse jewel, and safety mechanism form multiple layers. In Chaykin’s design, these elements are “spread out” in a single plane between two wheels whose rims mesh via peripheral teeth. They function as one system: the mass and moment of inertia of both wheels influence the frequency and isochronism of the oscillation, while the second, roller wheel interacts with the pallet fork. This reduces the overall height of the regulating organ without abandoning the Swiss lever escapement.

Another key innovation is an ultra-thin mainspring barrel without conventional top and bottom walls. From above it is retained by a bridge reinforced with stiffening ribs; from below, the watch case itself performs that role. The winding mechanism is relocated inside the barrel arbor, allowing the spring to sit on a single level rather than increasing the movement’s height. Worth separate mention is the strap with resilient titanium supports and elastic inserts: it forms part of the watch’s structural concept and significantly reduces unwanted stress on the extremely thin case.

What sets this watch apart from a mere “race for thinness” is that the master added rather than removed. Into a construction already pushed to the physical limit, he integrated a “mystery” display: the time is read on two fully transparent sapphire discs with no visible spokes, so the hour and minute indicators appear to float in mid-air. This innovative solution continues the historical lineage of “mystery” clocks—from the 19th-century table mechanisms of Jean-Eugène Robert-Houdin to Chaykin’s own “Mystery 1000 Jewels” of 2007.

One of the most complicated elements is the 1.65 mm-thin case itself, whose lower section serves as the mainplate of the in-house calibre. Despite its extreme slenderness, it must maintain precise geometry, high strength, and water resistance. For this reason, a special alloy is used—antimagnetic, hypoallergenic, and corrosion-resistant—introduced in watchmaking for the first time. Manufacturing a single case takes around two months and involves dozens of rigorous inspection stages.

The experimental concept has been translated into a repeatable production process. Each ThinKing Mystery watch is assembled and regulated entirely by hand, then subjected to a dedicated quality-control protocol.

watches.name: Récital 23

watches.desc:
A longstanding emblem of the BOVET collection, the Récital 23 is where haute horlogerie, the decorative arts, and high jewelry do more than coexist — they converse, in light. Its dial, entirely hand‑engraved, chiseled, and finished, becomes a living surface, catching and releasing radiance in a shimmer that answers the brilliance of its gem‑setting, a quiet yet eloquent testament to the Maison’s artisanal mastery.

The Recital 23 is housed in the “Writing Desk” case, which slopes from 12 o’clock to 6 o’clock, being thicker at 12 o’clock (12.8mm) than at 6 o’clock (8.6mm). This allows more space for the precision moon phase display and presents the time on the wrist.. Crafted in 18K red gold, the 43 mm x 38.70 mm case is adorned with 174 round‑cut diamonds (0.99 ct), complemented by 72 further diamonds on the bezel (1.00 ct), the cabochon crown, and the diamond‑set indices of the off‑set dial. Each stone is individually set to create a surface of extraordinary smoothness, so refined it passes the exacting “silk shirt” test without a whisper.

This year, the Récital 23 reveals a new dial expression. Hand‑chiseled and layered with lacquer, it opens onto a luminous, evolving depth of green — a color that evokes luxuriant gardens, tranquil horizons, and the warmth of long summer days that flow seamlessly into festive nights. Above this living tableau, the signature open‑worked hands drift with grace, forming a heart once every hour, a discreet, intimate gesture that belongs only to the wearer.

At 12 o’clock, the precision moon phase establishes a quiet dialogue between earth and sky. The moon, hand‑engraved to suggest its cratered relief and filled with luminescent material despite the complexity of its curved surface, appears within a three‑dimensional aperture that alone demands more than a day’s work to shape and decorate. Beneath this poetry lies a rigorous mechanism: so precise that the indication requires correction only once every 122 years.

Faithful to BOVET’s philosophy of meaningful, user‑focused complications, Pascal Raffy has integrated a push‑button directly into the real sapphire cabochon of the crown, allowing the moon phase to be adjusted with a simple, intuitive gesture, without any tools — an everyday luxury woven into a high complication.

Timeless yet expressive, the Récital 23 embodies the values that define BOVET: a devotion to hand‑crafted excellence, a profound respect for heritage, and an unceasing pursuit of artistic innovation in the art of measuring time.

watches.name: Serpenti Aeterna
watches.desc:
Sleek Expression of Gemsetting

Serpenti, the ultimate symbol of endless metamorphosis, evolves once again with Aeterna. This bold expression merges heritage with innovation, embracing a modern and futuristic vision while staying true to Bvlgari’s creative legacy. At its core, Aeterna reinterprets the snake’s monolithic form with striking purity. Its radically simplified design strips away the superfluous, revealing an essence of sculptural elegance. More than just a watch, Serpenti Aeterna is a true manifesto of style and modernity.

Designed as a bangle, it seamlessly stacks with other Bvlgari bracelets, allowing for infinite customization and personal expression. Featuring a 24 mm curved rose gold case and set with 293 round brilliant-cut diamonds, this creation redefines everyday elegance. Each diamond is meticulously snow-set, creating a shimmering pave that captures and reflects light with incomparable intensity. A true jewel of contemporary watchmaking that balances sophistication with modern ease, turning daily wear into a moment of refined expression.

watches.name: L'Heure du Diamant

watches.desc:
Seamless fluting, from dial to bracelet: heritage reinvented

Rounding out the collection, another white gold interpretation brings a new angle to the L’Heure du Diamant narrative. True to the collection’s identity, its silhouette is crowned by a diamond bezel, here adorned with pear‑shaped diamonds set. Its cushion‑shaped case is paired with a softly shimmering fluted white‑gold dial, from which the distinctive fluted texture continues seamlessly into the new integrated gold link bracelet, creating a unified visual flow. This supple bracelet design traces its origins to a historic creation from the Scheufele family workshops of the 1960s, reaffirming the Maison’s long‑standing expertise in precious‑metal craftsmanship. The dial is punctuated by black matte hands, whose crisp, minimalist lines introduce a graphic counterpoint that ensures immediate and intuitive reading of the time. Powered by the same in‑house mechanical movement that animates the onyx models presented earlier, the Chopard 09.01‑C, this model offers a novel expression of the collection’s blend of radiance, heritage, and meticulously honed craftsmanship.

watches.desc:
Triple Mystery Skeleton - The Art of Mystery in Motion

The Triple Mystery Skeleton represents the quintessence of jewellery haute horlogerie, where mechanical excellence meets the art of adornment in perfect harmony. Created around a system of rotating discs that are harmoniously set, and powered by a mechanism and movement developed in house, this timepiece transforms the reading of time into a captivating visual experience.

Franck Muller imagined a watch capable of defying traditional horological codes. The Triple Mystery follows the path opened by the Mystery, which replaced hands with a rotating disc, and the Double Mystery, which introduced two discs for the hours and minutes. This creation goes further by adding a third rotating disc dedicated to the seconds, bringing a new depth and rhythm to the perception of time.

Instead of conventional hands, hours, minutes and seconds are displayed through three rotating discs in continuous motion. The result is hypnotic and almost magical, as time appears to float across the dial. The diamond setting enhances this sensation, guiding the eye through a luminous composition where mechanical movement and jewellery craftsmanship become inseparable.

The technical challenge lies in driving three independent discs with precision, especially the seconds disc, whose rapid rotation requires extreme lightness, stability and energy control. The skeletonized architecture reveals the complexity of the mechanism while preserving the elegance and clarity of the display.

With the Triple Mystery Skeleton, Franck Muller unites high complication, jewellery artistry and visual poetry. More than a timepiece, it is a mechanical choreography of light, motion and mystery, expressing the Maison’s unique ability to turn time into emotion.

watches.name: Swinging Pebble
watches.desc: In 1972, Piaget created a collection of several Kimono pocket watches, playing with asymmetrical shapes, the colours of ornamental stones, and the sensuality of touch with this pebble shape that can be easily held in the hand. Today, Piaget celebrates that audacity with a contemporary reinterpretation, capturing the essence of the original while forging a new path forward. For Piaget, time has always been more than a measure, it’s also a movement, a rhythm, a dance. The Swinging Pebbles embody this philosophy once again : watches which celebrate shapes, craftsmanship, and freedom. The seamless harmony of gold, ornamental stones, and timekeeping reflects Piaget’s unrivaled mastery of each. Staying faithful to the original design, a carved and polished ornamental stone pebble frames a watch case that is perfectly nested within, a true demonstration of Piaget’s expertise in both watchmaking and high jewellery. Each pebble is sculpted from a single slice of stone, carefully selected for its colour, its unique veining, and its beautiful luster by Piaget’s internal gemologists. The challenge is even greater as the dial must flawlessly match the pebble case. Each pendant hangs from a sinuous, twisted gold chain, tribute to Piaget’s expertise in goldsmithing and chainmaking, a know-how internally mastered since the 60’s.

watches.name: Paradise Bird Toucan
specs: Jean Schlumberger by Tiffany / 10-pieces limited series
watches.desc:
The Toucan Paradise Bird watch is a horological interpretation of Jean Schlumberger's iconic Oiseaux de Paradis creations, bringing together Tiffany & Co.'s expertise in gemstones, enamel, sculpture and diamond-setting within a single miniature work of art.

Magnificent gemstones, exceptional enamel artistry and peerless gold sculpting and gem-setting combine to transform the watch into a miniature tropical tableau. Blending fantasy and natural beauty, a tiny gem-set toucan bird perches on a richly colored chalcedony cabochon that appears to float above a nature-inspired enamel dial. Crafted from three coats of hand-painted enamel foliage, resting on four layers of opaque blue enamel, the dial requires over 80 hours of high-precision work.

The 2.5-carat cabochon-cut chalcedony stone floats above an aperture in the dial that is aligned with a loupe on the caseback, allowing more light to pass through it, amplifying the color and visual depth. 

The 18k yellow gold body of the Paradise Bird Toucan is set with blue sapphires, tsavorites, white and yellow diamonds, and features a turquoise beak and pink sapphire eye. Set with a total of 69 stones (1 pink sapphire, 18 white diamonds, 4 yellow diamonds, 4 tsavorites, 41 blue sapphires and 1 turquoise) and combining the crafts of miniature sculpture and gem-setting, the Toucan is the result of 32 hours of meticulous craft. The vivid purple of its perch, a 2.5-carat cabochon-cut chalcedony stone, is complemented by the glowing blues and greens of the enamel background.

specs:
Manual-winding mechanical 
Power reserve: 100 h, 21600 vph

Dead-beat second on constant force
watches.desc:
With their new interpretation of the Constant Force Tourbillon 11 Platinum, Arnold & Son pay tribute to the watchmaking genius of the House’s founder. This platinum edition represents the final opus of the Constant Force 11 collection – launched with the gold model – and crowns the celebration of 260 years of heritage. It also celebrates the magic of nature with a dial ornamented with a hand-guilloché surface in the “tremblé” style, evoking the fern-covered moors around Tintagel in Cornwall – the birthplace of John Arnold and setting for the legendary adventures of King Arthur.

Adorned with new refinements, the Constant Force Tourbillon 11 was purposefully designed by Arnold & Son to honour the timepiece that Abraham-Louis Breguet presented to John Roger Arnold in 1808. Now conserved by the British Museum, this historic timepiece, based on John Arnold’s No. 11 chronometer, is believed to be the first tourbillon-regulated watch made by Abraham-Louis Breguet after he filed the patent in 1801.

A fern-covered dial

The Constant Force Tourbillon 11 platinum edition features a distinctive solid gold dial. The fine detail of the “tremblé” is expertly crafted by hand with a burin engraver. Under the controlled motion of the tool, the sharp tip has traced a succession of artfully irregular zigzags. This organic pattern is surprisingly harmonious and takes its inspiration from the wild moors of Cornwall, where ferns curl in fleeting arabesques as the sea winds blow. Each etched curve seems to capture the soul of this mystical land, the birthplace of John Arnold and home to Arthurian legends. The engraving weaves a poetic tie between the master’s watchmaking heritage and the elemental forces that shaped his childhood. The wind, the dancing ferns and the famous mists – all the magic of Cornwall – are reflected in the golden dial, transforming timekeeping into an ode to nature and history.

The dial is meticulously pierced to accommodate the white opal hour and minute subdial, as well as the mechanism delivering constant force to the tourbillon cage. The latter can be seen under an 18-carat gold bridge and rotates in exact, one-second increments. This rhythm is far from insignificant as it carries the legacy of marine chronometry when each second counted was a longitude reclaimed from the ocean.

A timekeeper’s testament

The classically shaped, rounded case measures 41.5 mm in diameter. Crafted in platinum, it appears exceptionally slender on the wrist. On the dial side, it is fitted with a delicate bezel framing a domed sapphire crystal with an anti-reflective coating on both sides. On the reverse, it features a sapphire case back through which the bridges and the tourbillon of the in-house manual winding A&S5219 calibre can be seen. Water resistant to 3 bar, the watch is worn on a hand-stitched midnight blue alligator leather strap, fastened with a platinum folding clasp.

A constant force mechanism

To ensure perfect isochronism throughout its 100-hour power reserve, Arnold & Son have positioned their patented constant force mechanism between the main gear train and the tourbillon. Visible on the dial, this ingenious system regulates the energy from the barrels, eliminating any variations in torque that could disturb the balance’s oscillation. Second after second, it rearms a finely adjusted spiral guaranteeing a completely stable transmission of energy to the tourbillon cage. The precise choreography of this constant force mechanism is magnified by an 18-carat gold bridge, emphasising the watchmaking excellence.

The constant force mechanism replaces the group of components known as the “fusée-and-chain” that John Arnold used in his chronometers. The advantage of this system is that it not only delivers a constant force to the regulating organ, it also produces a true-beat seconds display. The seconds are not indicated by a traditional seconds hand, but by the tip of the hand-blued anchor, which simultaneously serves as a structural bridge for the constant force mechanism.

A balanced tourbillon

This final limited series of 11 pieces pays tribute to the legendary friendship between John Arnold and Abraham-Louis Breguet. Its sapphire case back reveals the A&S5219 calibre, whose architecture is directly inspired by the first regulator with tourbillon created by Abraham-Louis Breguet. This chef-d'oeuvre, housed in the British Museum, was inspired by Arnold’s No. 11 chronometer and offered to his son in 1808. The Constant Force Tourbillon 11 revives this watchmaking bond: its tourbillon cage faithfully reproduces the original design. With extremely pure lines, the tourbillon features a distinctive and remarkably delicate linear, mirror-polished and rounded cage bridge, revealing a variable-inertia balance whose design draws on John Arnold’s most accomplished chronometers. In this true dialogue across time, every component speaks to the extraordinary union of two masters of timekeeping.

A celebration of friendship

The finishing of the main plate, bridge and tourbillon cock is virtually identical to that of the very first tourbillon. To complete the tribute, Arnold & Son have included hand-engraved inscriptions on the barrel bridge and added the famous plate on which another homage has been engraved: “To the revered memory of John Arnold and Abraham-Louis Breguet. Friends in their time, legendary watchmakers always.”. This inscription definitively gives the Constant Force Tourbillon 11 its place in a unique historical saga: one in which the friendship between two geniuses gave rise to some of the most remarkable advances in chronometry.

watches.desc:
DC6 Night Forest

The DC6 Night Forest is the brand’s lightest watch. It weighs 45 grams and is a limited edition of eight pieces. At the heart of the timepiece, a flying tourbillon tilted at a 30-degree angle completes one revolution in 60 seconds.

Originally, the tourbillon was designed for pocket watches, which spent their days motionless and upright, tucked into a vest. In this position, gravity always pulls on the balance wheel in the same way, causing it to run slow. By rotating on its axis, the tourbillon exposes the balance wheel to all angles and averages out the deviations. When held vertically, the watch is corrected. On the wrist, however, this is not the case: the arm is constantly moving and already compensates for gravity. The tourbillon is only useful when the watch is laid flat and motionless.

But a wristwatch is rarely placed upright, and when laid flat, the tourbillon rotates in a horizontal plane, where it no longer corrects anything. The 30-degree tilt then comes into play: it tilts the balance wheel away from the horizontal and restores the tourbillon’s corrective effect. The titanium cage, which houses the small seconds hand, is black—a color formed in the metal through micro-arc oxidation rather than applied as a coating, ensuring it will not fade.

The brand’s watches are recognizable by their distinctive shape and the concealed crown at 6 o’clock. The “Magic Crown” is retractable, composed of 31 components, and recedes into the case when not in use. Moving the crown from its usual position at 3 o’clock is what allows for the case’s symmetry and ergonomics, and it is the first element designed when a new caliber is developed.

The case of the DC6 Night Forest is made of carbon fiber, specifically a unidirectional variant where the fibers all run in the same direction, continuous along the entire length. This is the same carbon fiber used in aerospace structures and Formula 1, which is extremely durable. When held up to the light, the surface resembles veined wood, a far cry from the speckled appearance of forged carbon. These lines are inspired by the Risoux Forest, which lies directly across from the workshop. The carbon is framed by sloping lugs made of Grade 5 titanium. The movement is housed in a titanium chamber that ensures water resistance to 50 meters.

On the dial, two sapphire domes reveal the tourbillon, which rotates at 9 o’clock, facing the hemispherical hour and minute display at 3 o’clock. At 12 o’clock, the power reserve indicator—another complication of the timepiece—shows the movement’s 55-hour power reserve.

The largest portion of the dial is taken up by two titanium plates featuring the hand-engraved “Pointes du Risoux” guilloché pattern, inspired by the tips of trees in a forest as seen from the sky. They are not covered by a sapphire crystal, and the pattern can be felt under the finger just as clearly as it can be seen. The dial itself is topaz green—the hue of a mountain lake on a clear day—achieved by anodizing titanium that has been previously sunburst-finished. The smoky effect is a trompe-l’œil applied by hand using an airbrush. The numerals are applied in silver powder and stand out against the surface.

On the back, the titanium bridges are angled at 3° to create a cascade of light. Decorated entirely by hand, they meet the exacting standards of traditional watchmaking in the Vallée de Joux: Côtes du Solliat, polished chamfers and moldings, graining, hand engraving, and drawn flanks.

David Candaux is an independent watchmaker based in Solliat, in the Vallée de Joux, where watchmaking has been practiced since 1740. He founded his brand in 2017, after more than twenty years developing movements for some of the most demanding watchmakers. A watchmaker, manufacturer, and engineer, he designs and develops his watches, which are crafted using traditional methods with his small team in the workshop. He is the only watchmaker to construct each of his movements entirely from titanium.
