watches.name: Vox Temporis
specs:
Manual-winding mechanical 
Power reserve: 90 h, 21600 vph
watches.desc:
INSPIRED BY THE HISTORICAL TACT WATCH MADE BY LEROY IN 1810, L.LEROY HAS CREATED “VOX TEMPORIS” A TOURBILLON MINUTE REPEATER WITH ROTATING DIAL.

Founded in Paris in 1785 under Charles Leroy, himself the son of watchmaker, L.Leroy has written some of the finest chapters in the history of French watchmaking and chronometry, developing a wealth of technical and inventive treasures for over two centuries.

This human, artistic and industrial adventure is marked by illustrious names including Marie Antoinette, Proust, Matisse, Napoleon, Queen Victoria, Roosevelt, Chopin, Nobel, Bugatti, to mention but a few owners of a watch signed Leroy.

Faithful to its extraordinary and inimitable watchmaking heritage, L.Leroy has created the stunning “VOX TEMPORIS” inspired by a rare ancient pendant tact watch made by Leroy around 1810 for the Prince Emil Maximilian Leopold Augustof Hesse.

At that period, when electricity was unknown and luminous hands were not yet invented, this type of watch allowed the time to be read, even in the dark, by touching the hand that moved in the direction of the twelve diamonds on the periphery of the case, acting as indices.

In the 21st century, L.Leroy reinterprets this exquisite timepiece. A challenge that sees the Maison blend, in perfect harmony, its rich historical legacy with the demands of the contemporary era.

A unique and refined design

A watch with a very complex construction, both in terms of style and mechanics, which required the highly qualified skills of watchmaking technicians for the development and assembly of its manual winding movement,comprising a flying tourbillon and the minute repeater mechanism.Not forgetting the master engraver and the specialists in top-level finishing.

The case

The Officer’s-style case, measuring 43 mm in diameter, is crafted in Platinum.

“VOX TEMPORIS” is complemented by an Alligator strap (top and bottom) available in Black or dark Navy blue colour. It fastens to the wrist with an openworked round folding clasp, bearing the brand's interlaced double “L” logo.

An eye-catchingdial and a stunning calibre

“VOX TEMPORIS" features a unique and out-of-the-ordinary time display for a model from the 2000s, but legitimised by the historical piece from which it takes its inspiration. It has a rotating dial boasting a superlative flinqué soleil decoration with a translucent dark blue varnish finish. This pattern emanates near a perimeter point, where the rhodium-plated, arrow-shaped, hand-engraved hour hand is fixed and extends its rays around the circumference of the display.

When the dial rotates, the arrow-shaped hand points towards the hours.

To know the precise time, the minute repeater comes into action. This sophisticated mechanism, reputed to be the queen of complications, is developed on a hand-wound movement, which is also equipped with a flying tourbillon that improves its chronometric performance.

Once the repeater slide, positioned between 8:30 and 9:30, is activated, the time will be audible acoustically thanks to the finely tuned chiming mechanism. The design of the case has been meticulously studied and developed to amplify the different tones of the sound indicating the hours, quarters and minutes emitted by the two gongs struck by the two hammers, visible on the case back.

The powerful “engine” which drives this work of art is a hand-wound in-house calibre, consisting of 321 components, beating at a frequency of 3Hz/ 21.600 vibrations per hour. It comprises the minute repeater mechanism on two gongs, a single barrel guaranteeing 90-hour power reserve and the flying tourbillon which performs a complete rotation in one minute.

Lovers of fine watchmaking mechanics will be able to admire this amazing movement with its single bridge, and hand-bevelled edges, by opening the Platinum cover on the case backusing the discreet push-button at 4 o'clock.

“VOX TEMPORIS" once again testifies to the brand's technical expertise and its mastery of the art of decoration. A true joy for the lucky collector who, will enrich his collection with a unique masterpiece of time.

watches.name: Tambour Taiko Arty Automata
specs:
Self-winding mechanical 
Power reserve: 65 h, 28800 vph
watches.desc:
The Louis Vuitton Tambour Taiko Arty Automata redefines contemporary high watchmaking by elevating the automata and Grand Feu enamel to new heights. Inspired by the House’s artistic collaborations, its audacious dial is defined by an animated dialogue between form and perspective, conjuring a world of pure sensory vibrancy.

The dial of the Tambour Taiko Arty Automata is nothing short of an explosion of color and movement. Twenty miniature elements, arranged across four different levels, endow the watch with an extraordinary depth and dimension. The result of more than 250 hours of painstaking hand work, the dial is composed of 23 distinct shades of champlevé enamel. The LFT AU05.01 caliber and its rotor are finely decorated with motifs that echo the dial’s own visual narrative. The white gold rotor is rendered in miniature painting, a recognized specialty of La Fabrique des Arts.

As a final touch, a shimmering cascade of baguette-cut sapphires and rubies sweeps across the bezel, flooding the watch with color and light.

A press of the pusher at 8 o’clock sets the dial in motion, and seven interconnected animations unfold with the precision of a choreographed performance: four Monogram Flowers spin in alternating directions, the heart and eye flicker to life, and the word “LOVE” transforms into “MOVE”, as a call to action. The tourbillon, shaped as a peace symbol, turns with calm deliberation, one full revolution every minute. The watch is powered by the automatic LFT AU05.01 caliber, developed and crafted at the La Fabrique du Temps Louis Vuitton.

watches.name: Loco Classic
specs:
Manual-winding mechanical 
Power reserve: 144 h, 28800 vph
watches.desc:
The C1 Loco Classic represents the latest chapter in Christopher Ward’s Atelier series, continuing the brand’s pursuit of bringing the quality, creativity and emotional draw of haute horlogerie to as many people as possible.

Work on the project began in early 2024, before the launch of the integrated sports-focused C12 Loco, with a clear objective: to explore a parallel expression of the hand-wound CW-003. Starting from the movement’s raw architecture, Christopher Ward sought to create a refined dress watch combining the original, movement-led design and artisanal finishing that define the contemporary renaissance in high-end independent watchmaking.

While sharing its symmetrical layout with the C12 Loco, the C1 Loco Classic was conceived to evoke an entirely different emotion. Every visible component was reconsidered. New bridges, front and rear, adopt softer, more rounded forms and are embellished with more than five hours of hand-finishing. The work is carried out by APJ, a specialist based in the Swiss Jura.

This commitment to detail extends throughout the watch. A heavily domed ceramic time-telling dial features laser-etched, lacquer-filled Roman numerals and minute track, paired with diamond-polished lance hands subtly curved to follow the profile of the dial. Beneath, a deeply grained base dial is treated with a varnish containing powdered mother-of-pearl. Evenly distributed across the surface, the particles create a dense, finely textured shimmer that brings the backdrop to life.

These elements are housed within a 41mm Light-catcher™ case crafted in 904L stainless steel, chosen for its lustre. Combining high polish with fine brushing, the case measures just 8.55mm in height and is paired with double-domed sapphire crystals front and rear, resulting in a total thickness of 14.1mm. A distinctive scalloped groove introduces depth and definition to the case flanks before flowing into the lugs. Achieving this form requires each lug to be individually soldered to the case.

Watches of this ilk have traditionally prioritised artistry and finishing above outright performance. The C1 Loco Classic refuses that compromise. Maintaining a 4Hz beat rate, its bespoke free-sprung balance wheel, escape wheel and hairspring are driven by twin barrels that release energy simultaneously rather than sequentially. This approach produces a flatter torque curve, preserving amplitude and enabling accuracy of -0/+7 seconds per day throughout a category-leading six-day power reserve.

Named in recognition of its state of constant motion – and the audacity of creating a watch of this calibre at this price, at volume – the C1 Loco Classic represents a new expression of CW-003: one that combines the precision and reliability of a modern sports watch with the elegance, finishing and emotional appeal of contemporary haute horlogerie.

Presented in Oro, the C1 Loco Classic will be available from October 15th, 2026, with further launch colours and bracelet options to follow.

watches.name: Classic Worldtimer Manufacture
specs:
Self-winding mechanical 
Power reserve: 72 h, 28800 vph
watches.desc:
Since its launch in 2012, the Classic Worldtimer Manufacture has established itself as one of the flagship models of the Maison Frederique Constant and a new icon of contemporary watchmaking. A Swiss Made Haute Horlogerie timepiece, an ingenious function and high added value are the keys to its success, making this timepiece an emblematic model.

Today, the Maison revisits its flagship model. New Manufacture FC-719 movement. Power reserve extended to 72 hours. New 40 mm diameter case. New date-free, streamlined dial. With this new version of this iconic model, Frederique Constant takes a bold step.

An authentic Manufacture

At Frederique Constant, men and women work to create high added-value Swiss Made timepieces. This new FC-719 movement was designed within its workshops. The challenge was twofold: to maintain the reliability of its predecessor while at the same time improving its technical characteristics. The result? An impressive 35th Manufacture movement developed by Frederique Constant since its founding in 1988.

Not many Maisons under 40 years old have the boldness to pursue the ambition of becoming an authentic Swiss Made timepiece manufacturer. This passion echoes throughout the Frederique Constant workshops. It is here that movements are developed, prototyped, assembled and regulated. It is here that the watchmakers' skillful and controlled movements wield tweezers, screwdrivers and oilers to invent contemporary watchmaking.

An optimised movement

Behind its legibility and ease of use, the Classic Worldtimer Manufacture conceals a beautifully crafted horological complication. It offers a simultaneous, real-time display of the time in all 24 reference time zones. By opting for a two-colour disc, the traveller can intuitively distinguish between day and night time zones. On the new Classic Worldtimer Manufacture, the decision to forgo the date further enhances the legibility of the hours, minutes and the precious complication. This allows travellers, whether in body or spirit, to keep track of time wherever their journey takes them.

Developed on a proven technical basis, the Manufacture FC-719 movement has seen its power reserve optimised. Formerly 38 hours, it now has a capacity of 72 hours. This increase of approximately 90% provides a full three-day power reserve. This optimisation is made possible by a longer mainspring and a revised alloy composition. What’s more, not only does the FC-719 calibre maintain its original frequency of 4 Hz, but also, despite its larger mainspring, it fits into a case that is 2 mm smaller in diameter. The FC-719 therefore becomes one of the most optimised Worldtimers on the market.

A module that celebrates simplicity

How complicated it can sometimes be to make things simple! With only 24 components, the Worldtimer module is a perfect example. Take, for instance, the adjustment of all functions with a single crown. First advantage: practicality, since the user accesses all functions with just the crown.

Second advantage: reliability. No need for correctors and their fragile mechanical linkages. Especially since the stylus needed to press them is never readily available when travelling. Thirdly, water resistance. By eliminating various corrections and numerous openings in the case, the new Classic Worldtimer Manufacture guarantees water resistance to 5 ATM. The Manufacture also preserves the clean lines of the new 40 mm classic case.

A new chapter, true to the spirit of the Manufacture

By combining mechanical innovation, artisanal mastery, and contemporary design, Frederique Constant offers the Classic Worldtimer Manufacture a new chapter. It perfectly illustrates the Maison's ambition: to present high added-value Swiss Made timepieces. From the meticulously developed and hand-assembled FC-719 movement to the aesthetics and finishes of the dials, every detail testifies to the passion and daring of the Maison. With this reinterpretation of its iconic model, Frederique Constant confirms its identity as a modern Manufacture, capable of combining traditional know-how and contemporary watchmaking, offering travellers and fine watchmaking enthusiasts a timepiece of exceptional value.

watches.name: Noctograph by Massena LAB and Raúl Pagès
specs:
Manual-winding mechanical 
Power reserve: 60 h, 28800 vph
watches.desc:
Noctograph by Massena LAB and Raúl Pagès is a limited-edition wristwatch with a serene dial, elegant stainless steel case, and a proprietary movement designed by Massena LAB in collaboration with Raúl Pagès.

The Noctograph melds minimalism with the classical and historical influences referenced by Massena LAB. The dial is a dark and intriguing shade of blue, vertically brushed, shifting in the light from slate to petrol to deep midnight. The subtle "Massena" signature sits carefully placed at 4 o'clock.

Surrounding the dial is a bright rhodium-plated chapter ring, radially brushed and marked with a fine railroad track. At six o'clock, a second scale frames the small seconds counter, subtly sunken below the main dial. Floating above are a pair of feuille hands in stainless steel, drawn from the dress watches of the 1930s and 1950s, in quiet contrast with the dial's modernist character.

Noctograph by Massena LAB and Raúl Pagès is powered by the caliber M660, a movement designed by Raúl Pagès in collaboration with Massena LAB, manually wound and Swiss-made with a power reserve of 60 hours. Visible through the sapphire crystal caseback, it features a broad plate with Côtes de Genève finishing and hand-chamfered plates and bridges. Raúl Pagès' signature mark, taking the form of a tortoise in reference to his celebrated automaton, is tucked beneath the balance wheel, carefully framed by overlapping circles of perlage.

This level of finishing demands an elevated blend of artistry and skill, typically reserved for timepieces commanding three times the price. Pagès personally oversees and directs production of the M660, though he does not engage directly in the production or decoration of the movement. Execution is entrusted to a select group of Swiss watchmakers working to his vision.

The Noctograph is housed in a 38.5mm stainless steel case with architecture inspired by dress watches from the 1940s and 50s, brushed on its sides with polished lugs and bezel. The watch is fitted with a handmade dove grey leather strap with a stainless steel pin buckle.

Noctograph by Massena LAB and Raúl Pagès is limited to 99 pieces.

watches.name: MING × J.N. Shapiro 37.06 Lightning
specs:
Manual-winding mechanical 
Power reserve: 42 h, 28800 vph
watches.desc:
A New Collaboration

The MING × J.N. Shapiro 37.06 Lightning is a joint project between Horologer MING and J.N.Shapiro, two founding members of the Alternative Horological Alliance (AHA), and the product of a long-running friendship between Ming Thein and Josh Shapiro.

It began with a shared desire to create something together, and a simple question: What happens when two independent makers bring their own forms of handwork to the same dial?

From Los Angeles To Kuala Lumpur

The answer begins in Los Angeles, inside Josh Shapiro’s workshop. Every Lightning dial is crafted from grade-2 titanium and individually engine-turned by hand on a traditional rose-engine lathe using a pattern called “Lightning guilloché.” This marks the first time a wristwatch by Josh Shapiro has used this specific pattern, creating a hypnotic texture that gives the surface a sense of dynamism that feels right at home with MING. The material and pattern both demand precision, and the guilloché process carries a high failure rate. It is slow, precise, tactile work, and it sets the stage for everything that follows.

From California, the dials travel to Kuala Lumpur, where Ming Thein heat-colors each dial with a handheld butane torch. The process transforms the dial into a polychromatic field of deep blue, rich purple, and vibrant orange-yellow. The unique coloration does not depend on paint, lacquer, or any additional surface coating – only heat, timing, restraint, and creative license.

There is very little room for error when heating the dials. Just a few seconds too long or too short with the torch can create uneven color distribution and ruin the dial entirely. Even with perfect control of the torch, the guilloché process can expose variations in the titanium’s crystalline structure that compromise the final result. The failure rate is high, with only about one in every three dials making it into a finished watch. The dials that make the cut are never exactly alike, with each final color gradient unique to that particular dial. Lightning, after all, never strikes twice.

This synergistic process makes the 37.06 Lightning more personal than the typical watch collaboration. Josh Shapiro and his team engine-turn every dial by hand, and Ming Thein personally heat-colors each one by hand. They both leave their creative fingerprints on the Lightning’s most visible element. As a result, production of the 37.06 Lightning is naturally constrained by the craftsmanship involved, even though the watch is not a limited-edition release.

Beyond The Dial

The Lightning dial is housed in MING’s familiar 37-series case, crafted here from 316L stainless steel. Measuring 38mm in diameter, 10.9mm in thickness, and 44.5mm lug-to-lug, the case is designed to maximize dial presence while preserving real-world wearability. Its narrow bezel allows the Lightning to wear visually larger and thinner than the dimensions suggest, while the sculpted lug profile requires multi-axis machining to flow cleanly from the case flanks into the lugs.

The 37.06 Lightning is topped by a domed sapphire crystal with laser-hollowed cavities filled with Super-LumiNova X1® (SLN), which serve as indices. The hour and minute hands receive multiple applications of SLN X1 for a more even, longer-lasting glow. There is no seconds hand, keeping the timekeeping display focused and uninterrupted.

Inside is the manual-wind Sellita for MING calibre SW210.M1, a MING-exclusive execution with skeletonized, rhodium-plated bridges and an anthracite-coated baseplate. The power reserve is approximately 42 hours. The watch is sealed with domed sapphire crystals on the front and back, both with double-sided anti-reflective coating, and offers 100 meters of water resistance.

Hours, Minutes, Seconds, Retrograde Minutes, Jumping hours 
Slow return of hands
watches.desc:
OTSUKA LOTEC is a Japanese watch brand founded by the independent watchmaker Jiro Katayama.

Inspired by mixing consoles, the No.8 shows, once every hour, a variety of functions operate together beneath the crystal ── the hour channel jumping in a single motion, while the minute fader, linked to the flywheel, returns from 60 minutes to 0. Through the side of the crystal, the motion of the minute fader unfolds between the two-layered dial, as a seconds disk above remains in constant rotation at one revolution every 90 seconds.

The No. 8 features a MIYOTA movement with an in-house module. The module is composed of 62 components and uses one ultra-small 1.5 mm ball bearing manufactured by MinebeaMitsumi, currently the smallest in the world, as well as two additional 2.5 mm ball bearings.

watches.name: Monaco Chronograph
specs:
Self-winding mechanical 
Power reserve: 80 h, 28800 vph
watches.desc:
The TAG Heuer Monaco Chronograph embodies the next generation of one of the most iconic watches in contemporary watchmaking. More than fifty years after its creation, the TAG Heuer Monaco reinvents itself while preserving its distinctive identity. This timepiece retains the design codes that made it legendary, with its unique square silhouette, crown positioned on the left, and a DNA deeply linked to motor racing, all while adopting a resolutely modern approach to ergonomics, comfort, and performance. Lighter, more dynamic, and more refined, this new interpretation was designed to offer a superior wearing experience, while preserving the bold character that has always distinguished the TAG Heuer Monaco.

This evolution is primarily reflected in completely redesigned aesthetics. Faithful to the famous reference associated with Steve McQueen, the watch features its signature opaline blue dial, contrasting silver sub-dials, and red accents inspired by the world of motor racing. But behind this iconic livery lies a deeply modernized architecture. Crafted in grade 5 titanium, the 39mm square case gains lightness and comfort, while its new proportions, sharper lines, and sculpted surfaces enhance its presence on the wrist. The sapphire crystal adopts a geometry closer to a perfect square, while the redesigned caseback better follows the curve of the wrist. Every detail is optimized, ensuring the TAG Heuer Monaco is more ergonomic, better balanced, and more pleasant for daily wear.

At the heart of this timepiece beats the Calibre TH20-11, an automatic chronograph movement that marks a significant step in the evolution of the collection. Developed in-house, it reinterprets the legacy of the legendary Calibre 11 while meeting contemporary performance standards. Its bi-compax architecture, combined with the crown positioned on the left and the date at 6 o'clock, ensures clear and perfectly balanced readability. With an 80-hour power reserve and covered by a five-year warranty, the Calibre TH20-11 offers a high level of reliability and precision. With this new generation of the TAG Heuer Monaco, the Maison achieves a masterful evolution of its icon: ever-contemporary, better performing, and always faithful to its avant-garde spirit.

watches.name: La Pièce No.2
specs:
Self-winding mechanical 
Power reserve: 46 h, 28800 vph
watches.desc:
Born from the collaboration between Beaubleu and the Monnaie de Paris, La Pièce n°2 Argent explores uncharted territory in watchmaking: a monobloc dial, engraved and struck directly from a single piece of metal. This world first achievement stems from the historic expertise of the millennium old Parisian institution, applied here for the very first time to the horological world.

Through the art of coin striking, the components of the dial, traditionally applied separately, fuse into a single, cohesive piece. Polished interiors, indices formed directly from the solid mass, interacting reliefs, and varied surface textures come together in a true technical tour de force, unprecedented for a monobloc dial.

Featuring mirror polished, satin, powdered, or iridescent finishes, each texture interacts with light to reveal the depth of the silver dial and the subtlety of its contours. Beaubleu’s signature floating second hand glides gracefully above, punctuating a metallic landscape that feels almost architectural.

Struck in the heart of Paris, La Pièce n°2 Argent embodies the convergence of historic craftsmanship, technical innovation, and contemporary watch design.

watches.name: Angles Guichets
specs:
Manual-winding mechanical 
Power reserve: 42 h, 21600 vph
watches.desc:
Earthly and celestial. Beda’a presents the Angles Guichets, the first Angles with a complication: a 24‑hour aperture display, with day and night indicated by the passage of the Sun and the Moon indicators. Poetic in intent yet precise in execution, the mechanism is manually wound and housed in a 37 mm case that has become the cornerstone of Beda’a’s offerings, an eight‑faceted body with integrated lugs, structured across three stepped levels.

The Angles Guichets pushes the Angles aesthetic further through one of the most demanding exercises in watch design: the aperture display. The upper aperture displays the hours on a fixed scale from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m. The Sun then the Moon travel across the opening, indicating the passage of day and night. Their motion is slow, almost imperceptible, intimating a different relationship with time.

The lower aperture is dedicated to the minutes. Here, Beda’a introduces a characteristic inversion: as the minute disc advances, a fine arrow set flush with the dial marks the reading point, reinforcing clarity while maintaining visual restraint.

On the movement side, the Angles Guichets retains the hand-wound Peseux/ETA 7001 calibre as a base. This time, however, to allow the timekeeping narrative to unfold across 24 hours, the gear train was revised so that it runs at half the usual speed — completing a full rotation in 24 hours instead of 12, while preserving a 42-hour power reserve. Those revisions were made without compromise to the calibre’s celebrated slimness, keeping the Angles Guichets to just 6.3 mm in thickness, giving the watch a balanced profile on any wrist.

watches.name: Chief Skeleton
specs:
Self-winding mechanical 
Power reserve: 41 h, 28800 vph 
Skeleton movement
watches.desc: The Chief Skeleton marks the first fully skeletonised timepiece in Favre Leuba’s 289-year history. Housed within the collection’s distinctive cushion-shaped case, its openworked architecture is defined by the custom-designed FLS01 calibre. Finished in 4N18 gold and framed by a vibrant blue minute track, the movement reveals a multi-layered composition centred around a semi-exposed barrel at 12 o’clock and a visible balance wheel at 6 o’clock. Balancing technical expression with refined proportions, the Chief Skeleton transforms mechanical watchmaking into a study of depth, light, and architectural design.

watches.name: Classics Moneta Handwinding
specs:
Manual-winding mechanical 
Power reserve: 63 h, 28800 vph
watches.desc:
The Classics Moneta collection has swiftly established itself as the new benchmark of Frederique Constant’s offering. The Manufacture has chosen to give the collection a new mechanical, vintage-inspired charm. The new Classics Moneta Handwinding introduces a 38.5 mm case and is powered by a hand-wound movement developed by La Joux-Perret, delivering an impressive 63-hour power reserve. Its smoked salmon gradient dial is paired with a vintage-style alligator leather strap featuring a small-scale pattern, creating an elegant and distinctly neo-retro aesthetic. Produced in a limited edition of just 999 pieces, this new model is available for under CHF 2,000.

No one can predict what will make a collection successful. Yet one thing is certain: since its launch in 2024, the Classics Moneta has made a striking impression. Its greatest strength lies in the geometry of its case. A watch case is typically distinguished by its shape or finishing. Here, the secret lies in the inner rehaut, whose profile is subtly sculpted with fluting reminiscent of the edge of a coin – the detail that inspired its name. The aesthetic is both familiar and distinctive, showcasing a traditional hallmark of fine watchmaking in an unexpected location on the case, creating a striking sense of originality.

The same balance defines this first mechanical edition, limited to just 999 pieces: a carefully judged harmony between the finest elements of contemporary watchmaking and the inspiration of the great classics of the last century.

First mechanical movement

The first notable development is the introduction of the collection’s first mechanical movement. Produced by La Joux-Perret in La Chaux-de-Fonds, Switzerland, and customised exclusively for Frederique Constant, it is a finely crafted hand-wound calibre.

Visible through the sapphire case back, the movement is adorned with Côtes de Genève decoration, a fitting tribute to Frederique Constant’s Genevan heritage. At its centre is the coat of arms that the brand has proudly displayed since 1988. On the opposite side of the movement sits the escapement, beating at 28,800 vibrations per hour (4 Hz) to ensure excellent chronometric stability. At the other end, part of the generously sized barrel is visible, providing the new Moneta with an impressive 63-hour power reserve. The choice of a hand-wound calibre not only allows its finishing to be fully appreciated, unobstructed by an oscillating weight, but also helps preserve the watch’s slim profile and neo-retro character, remaining true to the charm of the 1950s.

A unique dial

Among the watch’s vintage-inspired features, the new dial stands out most prominently. It showcases a subtle smoked salmon gradient, transitioning to deep black around the edges. This darker outer ring allows the applied, mirror-polished hour markers to stand out more clearly, ensuring excellent legibility. In keeping with its distinctly neo-retro character, the Moneta features two central dauphine hands, complemented by a small seconds display at 6 o’clock. Together, they follow the classic design codes of 1950s watchmaking, combining simplicity with timeless vintage elegance.

Finally, Frederique Constant has taken this aesthetic exercise to its conclusion with a new black alligator leather strap featuring small-scale patterning, offering both superior suppleness and a patinated look. The result is a well-balanced composition that gives contemporary watchmaking a piece imbued with a delightfully vintage refinement and strong added value.

watches.name: King Seiko VANAC
specs:
Self-winding mechanical 
Power reserve: 72 h, 28800 vph
watches.desc:
Introduced in 1972, the King Seiko VANAC series expressed a bold and unconventional spirit through its use of vibrant colors and a multifaceted design. Reinterpreted for today, the VANAC embodies King Seiko’s philosophy of “The Newest Classic,” blending heritage with a distinctly modern sense of individuality.

Amazing lightness meets powerful design

Since its inception, VANAC has been dedicated to the exploration of new possibilities. In this latest creation, this distinctive spirit is expressed through the introduction of titanium—a material that naturally aligns with the series’ bold and sporty character. Its distinctive luster and exceptional lightness create a striking contrast between the watch’s powerful, multifaceted form and its effortless feel on the wrist, offering a fresh and unexpected wearing experience.

The dynamic energy of modern Tokyo

Inspired by Tokyo’s cityscape and the highways that run through it, the design captures the perspective of a driver moving confidently toward an open horizon. Horizontal lines intersect with radiating patterns across the dial, evoking roads that stretch and converge in the distance while conveying a sense of speed, depth, and direction.

Within this vision, the dial reflects one of the defining scenes of this journey—the serene moment at dawn when the city gradually emerges in the morning light. The purple tone captures this quiet transition, subtly shifting with changing light while complementing the bold geometry of the case.

The bezel-less case and seamlessly integrated bracelet reinforce a sense of fluid continuity, while carefully refined finishing techniques ensure crisp edges and distortion-free surfaces, preserving the clarity of the design in titanium.

A movement at the forefront of Seiko’s mechanical craftsmanship

Powered by the automatic Caliber 8L45, the watch offers a 72-hour power reserve and the durability required for modern daily wear. Dynamic in expression and effortless in comfort, the titanium VANAC presents a contemporary interpretation of sporty refinement perfectly suited to today’s King Seiko collection.

watches.name: SpaceOne X Baltic - Seconde Majeure
specs:
Self-winding mechanical 
Power reserve: 42 h, 28800 vph
watches.desc:
The Seconde Majeure features an ingenious architecture built around its signature complication. A jumping-hour module—developed by Théo Auffret—is composed of three visible components.

Beneath the minute disc lies the Central Driving Wheel, which completes one full rotation every 60 minutes. At the end of each rotation, it engages with the Hour Star. Directly connected to the hour disc, this star features 12 teeth, each corresponding to one of the 12 hours.

Visible on the left, the Jumper Spring applies constant pressure to the Hour Star, keeping it perfectly indexed. It is also responsible for the instantaneous hour jump. As the Hour Star begins to rotate, the spring gradually builds tension. The hour changes the instant the spring snaps into the next tooth.

Both functional and decorative, the dial unifies the entire construction. Machined from a single piece of German silver, it serves as the main plate for the jumping-hour module while providing the structural foundation required for the movement to operate.

watches.name: Table Waltz Tourbillon Mirror Edition
specs:
Manual-winding mechanical 
Power reserve: 168 h, 18000 vph 
Skeleton movement

Hours, Minutes 
Chime on the hour (can be locked)
watches.desc:
The Table Waltz Tourbillon introduced the first tourbillon created in Vienna in more than a century. With the Mirror Edition, Carl Suchy & Söhne presents a pièce unique that further develops this contemporary interpretation of Austrian haute horlogerie.

Conceived as a horological object at the intersection of design, craftsmanship and mechanical innovation, the Table Waltz Tourbillon reflects a distinctly Viennese understanding of time. Rather than functioning solely as an instrument for measurement, it transforms time into a visible performance of movement, rhythm and sound.

At its core is the CS-T-1 tourbillon movement, developed and manufactured entirely in Austria. Composed of more than fifty individual components, the tourbillon rotates continuously on its own axis, introducing a dynamic visual dimension while representing one of watchmaking’s most demanding mechanical disciplines. Positioned as the focal point of the composition, it transforms technical precision into an ever-changing choreography of motion.

The case is milled from a single block of brass, subsequently nickel plated and finished with a lacquered surface. In contrast, the movement, tourbillon, and silver bell are rhodium plated, giving the mechanism a cooler, mirror-like presence that sharpens its definition and enhances its structural depth.

Designed by Rainer Mutsch and realised by master watchmaker Therese Wibmer, the Table Waltz Tourbillon combines architectural clarity with mechanical precision. The movement is framed by hand-cut and hand-engraved crystal panels developed in collaboration with the Viennese glassmaker J. & L. Lobmeyr, offering an unobstructed view of both the tourbillon and the striking mechanism.

Bringing together Austrian watchmaking, Viennese design and traditional craftsmanship, the Table Waltz Tourbillon Mirror Edition reinterprets a historic discipline for the present day. It stands as a contemporary expression of Vienna’s enduring contribution to the culture of time, where technical mastery and artistic refinement form a single, coherent whole.

watches.name: The Beehive Chiming Table Clock
specs: Mineral glass, brass & stainless steel, gold

Self-winding mechanical 
Power reserve: 192 h, 18000 vph
watches.desc:
A mechanical wonder honours three decades of Chopard Manufacture in Fleurier, bringing one of its symbols to life.

To mark the 30th anniversary of its Manufacture in Fleurier, Chopard presents The Beehive Chiming Table Clock in a limited series of 10 pieces, developed in collaboration with L’Épée 1839. Conceived as a chiming mechanical table clock and an Objet d’Art, this creation brings together horological innovation, Haute Joaillerie craftsmanship, and a powerful symbolic heritage.

The beehive has been a defining emblem of Chopard since the era of founder Louis-Ulysse Chopard in the 19th century, symbolizing precision, industriousness, and collective skill. Revived in 1996 by Karl-Friedrich Scheufele alongside the creation of Chopard Manufacture, this symbol finds a new expression in this creation. Its sculptural form, crafted in borosilicate glass with gold bees, evokes the harmony of a perfectly ordered hive.

The clock features rotating glass discs for the indication of hours and minutes, and a refined chiming mechanism with a glass bell gong. Three fixed bee motifs adorn the clock, symbolizing three generations of the Scheufele family. Made of 18-carat Ethical yellow gold in Chopard’s Haute Joaillerie atelier, each one is set with yellow sapphires, black and white diamonds, black spinels, and rock crystal.

Three chiming modes are displayed on the selector: active (ON), silent (OFF) and on demand (DEM).

For ease of use, the selector switches only between active and silent modes. In active mode, the Beehive Table Clock automatically chimes the number of hours on the hour, and once during the half hours. When set to silent, the chime is completely de-activated. In either mode, the selector can be manually rotated to activate the chime on demand, which will denote the number of hours of the current time. Upon release, the spring-loaded mode selector instantaneously returns to the previously selected mode (active or silent).

In its fantasies of mechanical creatures, L’Epée 1839 turns to nature with The Gekko, a sculptural timepiece powered by an openworked in-house 8-day skeleton movement and shaped after one of nature’s most surprising lizards.

Both timepiece and artistic object, The Gekko inhabits its surroundings like a living sculpture, bringing quiet mechanical life to the space it occupies. Designed for versatility, The Gekko by L’Epée 1839 can be mounted on a wall or placed on a table, allowing time to be read either as a wall clock or as a table clock. Once mounted on the wall, its attachment system allows the piece to be fixed in ten different positions, enabling the creature to adopt a variety of orientations - climbing, stretching, resting, upwards, downwards, sideways, or at an angle. In a clever extension of this adaptability, the hour markers can be repositioned thanks to a rotating dial ring, ensuring optimal legibility from any angle and allowing the object to adapt not only to its environment, but also to the vision of its owner.

Through the vision of designer Marie Siebenborn, L’Epée 1839 transforms this humble companion into a refined horological object. Small, silent, and ever watchful, the gekko has long captured the human imagination. Across cultures - from Southeast Asia to the Mediterranean and the islands of Polynesia - it is seen as a guardian of the home, a symbol of renewal, adaptability, and quiet resilience.

With The Gekko, L’Epée 1839 brings together mechanical craftsmanship, sculptural design, and functional versatility in a timepiece that can change position, perspective, and presence while remaining unmistakably alive in spirit.

watches.desc:
A NEW HOROLOGICAL CONCEPT
COSMO introduces a new horological concept: an entire mechanism, magnetically suspended and rotating continuously on its own axis.

ONE REVOLUTION, MULTIPLE DISPLAYS
COSMO's 14.5-kilogram mechanism completes one revolution on its own axis every sidereal day.
The relative motion of its components rotating at different speeds generates a complete array of time, calendar and astronomical indications.
COSMO simultaneously displays for a specific location on Earth:
Standard Time – Solar Time – Day – Date – Month – Zodiac – Sunrise – Sunset – Dawn – Dusk – Twilight – Apparent Position of the Sun and Stars – Daylight Saving Time.

TWO ECCENTRIC GEARS – ONE PATENT - 406 DAYS
The patented transmission system based on only two eccentric gears forms the foundation of COSMO's entire mechanical architecture.
Directly powered by the mainspring, it drives:

  • the mono-component flexure-based remontoire;
  • the large low-frequency escapement regulated by a 70 mm magnetically suspended balance wheel;
  • the continuous rotation of the entire mechanism.

The patented system delivers 406 days of power reserve from a single winding despite these exceptional energy demands.
The system is also designed to directly integrate the stopwork mechanism and the power reserve indicators.

THE DOME: USER INTERFACE AND ACOUSTIC RESONATOR
Far more than an exquisite handcrafted enclosure, the hand-blown Murano glass dome serves as a user interface to wind and to set COSMO.
It also reveals the astronomical indications and the luminous stars visible above a specific location at a precise moment.
At the owner's request, the dome acts as an acoustic resonator, amplifying the beating of the energy-optimised escapement and making it audible.

BEATING AT YOUR HEART RATE
COSMO’s flying escapement can be configured to beat at the owner's resting heart rate.

COSMO
A search for impossible simplicity.

watches.desc:
Louis Vuitton and De Bethune join forces to present the third chapter in Louis Vuitton’s ongoing journey through independent watchmaking, the LVDB-03 Louis Varius Project. From the close collaboration of La Fabrique du Temps Louis Vuitton and Master Watchmaker Denis Flageollet, the co-founder of De Bethune, comes a project that brought together thirty specialists – from fifteen different technical and artistic disciplines – to focus on a shared challenge: reinterpreting the “sympathique” mechanism. Now, two exceptional time objects embody the grandeur of this effort: a “sympathique” clock paired with an exclusive version of De Bethune’s DB25 GMT Starry Varius watch, whose movement is housed in a blued titanium Louis Vuitton Tambour Taiko case.

At the heart of the LVDB-03 Sympathique Louis Varius is a key-wound movement manufactured entirely by De Bethune. Comprising 763 components and equipped with two large barrels and a remontoir d’égalité, the in-house caliber delivers outstanding stability and autonomy. Beating at 18,000 vibrations per hour (2.5 Hz), it offers an impressive 11-day power reserve. The LVDB-03 GMT Louis Varius watch, powered by the De Bethune-designed DB2507LV calibre, is centrally placed in the clock by simply opening the strap and setting the timepiece in the designated compartment. It then enters into “sympathie”, by way of its crown, with the clock’s mechanism, which automatically winds the watch every ten hours and recalibrates its display every two hours if it differs from the clock by +/- seven minutes.

The clock’s architecture is inspired by the aesthetic codes of Louis Vuitton’s Tambour design, reinterpreting the iconic case shape. The double-sided, complementary hour markers are reproduced on the clock dial. De Bethune’s own signatures are also found on the dial: crafted from polished, blued titanium, a House hallmark, it is decorated with a starry sky and De Bethune’s emblematic Milky Way.

Anchored to a titanium base that is decorated with a marquetry of blued meteorite, the clock can be set in multiple orientations, a reference to the adjustable presentation of historical marine chronometers. In its reference position, the clock measures 310 mm in width, 266 mm in depth, and 260 mm in height. When inclined, its maximum height extends to 313 mm, offering versatility in display.

The most poetic feature on the clock was collaboratively created by Denis Flageollet and Belgian illustrator François Schuiten, an artist with a fantastic imaginary world: three panoramas, inspired by 19th-century dioramas and hand-engraved on rings of 5N rose gold. These miniature landscapes, each an ode to the Louis Vuitton Art of Travel, were hand-executed by Master Engraver Michèle Rothen and cover nearly a full meter of surface area: a steam train crossing a viaduct, hot-air balloons floating above the African savannah, sherpas climbing steep peaks. These golden scenes encircle the mechanism and slowly rotate, creating a sublime sense of the circular, cyclical nature of time. Crowning the clock is a decorative dome, also in rose gold, that features a hand-engraved image of the constellation Hercules, a subtle nod to the astrological sign of Louis Vuitton’s founder.

Sheltered by a polished titanium trunk inspired by the iconic Louis Vuitton Trophy Trunk and crafted by the House’s artisans within the historic Asnières workshop, the “sympathique” clock is one of the most exclusive and unique objects ever produced by Louis Vuitton and De Bethune.

The clock is presented together with the watch in order to illustrate the “sympathique” function. The indicated retail price therefore includes both the cost of the clock and that of the watch.

watches.desc:
The Frog Queen – Table Clock – Miki Eleta 2026

The table clock ‘The Frog Queen’ is an is a tribute to the garden as an oasis of calm that offers peace and inspiration.

Changes in the garden indicate the passing of time: every hour, a frog appears. The Frog Queen, hidden within a flower, reveals herself every twelve hours.

A crane lurks in the pond. Once in twelve hours, it pecks at the frogs. The flower immediately closes protectively around the Queen. The frogs hide beneath their lotus leaves.

On the hand-skeletted dial, richly decorated with snakes, flowers and tadpoles, a snake indicates the minutes. Each minute is represented by a tadpole.

The clock features many motifs from the Asian region. For instance, the number 8 is hidden throughout.

The days of the week on the hand-skeletted ring are represented by symbols for the sun, moon and the five elements: Moon (Monday), Fire (Tuesday), Water (Wednesday), Wood (Thursday), Metal (Friday), Earth (Saturday) and Sun (Sunday).

A mechanical automaton enhances the experience: fish and swans swim past on the outer ring, and water splashes from the upper pond onto the lower level. The automaton is wound by hand and runs for 15 minutes.

All parts of the clock and all the animals and plants (except for the glass figures) were handcrafted by Miki Eleta.
